name: Ethical Purchasing Group - SIA Project 22 23
description:
The system supports the management of an Ethical Purchasing Group (EPS), known in Italian as a Gruppo di Acquisto Solidale (GAS), associated with a km-zero fruit and vegetable store. The purpose of the system is to connect groups of customers with local farmers and store employees, supporting a conscious purchasing process based on knowledge of product origin, quality, characteristics, availability, and price.

The operating cycle of the purchasing group is organized on a weekly basis. Farmers provide estimates of the products they can supply between Friday at noon and Saturday morning. For each available product, farmers specify the product type, quantity, price, and optionally additional crop characteristics such as size, quality, or ripeness.

The information system maintains a catalogue of products containing descriptions, photographs, the unit of measurement used for sale, and the minimum and maximum quantities that can be ordered. Each availability entered by a farmer refers to one of the products contained in the catalogue.

Customers can browse the offers provided by the different farmers and place orders by selecting products and specifying the desired quantities. Customers are representatives of purchasing groups, such as families or groups of people, and only the registered representative of each group can submit an order.

Orders can be entered directly by customers through the web system or by store employees on behalf of customers. Before an order can be confirmed, the system checks that the quantities selected respect the minimum order constraints defined for each product. If the minimum quantities are not met, the customer must modify the order. After completion, the system sends an order summary to the customer by email.

Customer orders initially remain in an entered state until farmers confirm the actual quantities available by Monday morning. If the available quantities are sufficient to satisfy all orders, the orders are confirmed. When the available quantity of a product is insufficient, the system applies precedence rules based on customer priority and removes unavailable quantities from lower-priority orders.

Orders modified because of limited product availability are placed in a modified state and must be reviewed and explicitly accepted by customers. If every product in an order becomes unavailable, the order is cancelled.

After farmers confirm product availability, the system automatically performs payment for the quantities actually included in the order. Payments are made through a personal virtual wallet associated with each customer. Customers can recharge their wallet through the store at any time.

If a customer's wallet balance is insufficient immediately after order placement, the customer receives an email warning, but the order remains valid. If the balance is insufficient when the automatic payment is executed, the customer receives an SMS and has until Monday evening to recharge the wallet. If the required balance is still unavailable at that time, the order is cancelled.

Once payment has been successfully completed, customers can reserve a time slot for collecting their products from the store. Store employees can view the pickup schedule at the beginning of their shifts and prepare the packages corresponding to customer orders. When a customer arrives, the employee confirms the collection of the order.

If a customer fails to collect the order at the scheduled time, the system sends an SMS reminder. If the order has not been collected by Friday, the order is marked as forfeited and the customer's fair-play score is updated.

Farmers deliver their products to the store by Tuesday evening. Store employees confirm the receipt of the delivered quantities. If the goods have not arrived by 4 p.m. on Tuesday, the system sends an SMS reminder. If the goods have still not been delivered by 8 p.m., the related customer orders are updated, the missing amount is credited back to the affected customers with an additional 20 percent bonus, and the customers are informed of the delivery problem.

The system maintains a fair-play score for each customer. The score represents the reliability of the customer with respect to previous orders and is used as a precedence criterion when product availability is insufficient. The score is computed from the number of completed orders, reminders received, forfeited pickups, and modified orders. Customers with higher fair-play scores are given precedence over customers with lower scores when limited quantities must be allocated among competing orders.

highLevelGoals: Enable customers to make informed purchasing decisions by providing detailed information about product origin, quality, and availability.
Support the weekly purchasing cycle by enabling customers to place orders, manage modifications, and prioritize based on fair-play scores during limited availability.
Allow customers to pay for orders using a personal virtual wallet, with flexible recharge options and clear notifications for insufficient balances.
Ensure customers can schedule and complete product pickups with reminders and forfeiture mechanisms to maintain system reliability.
Allow farmers to submit product availability estimates and enable the system to manage allocation based on real-time availability and customer priority.
Notify customers of delivery delays and automatically credit back payments with bonuses when goods are not delivered by the deadline.
Enable store employees to manage orders, process payments, schedule pickups, and handle delivery confirmations with automated reminders and status updates.
Track and reward customer reliability through a fair-play score system to ensure equitable allocation during product shortages.
Provide mechanisms for customers to receive notifications, modify orders, and be informed of system actions such as cancellations or bonuses.
lowLevelGoals: Customer accesses a product page to view its origin, quality certifications, and availability status.
Customer submits an order request for a specific product with quantity and delivery preferences.
Customer updates an order by changing quantity, delivery time, or cancellation request.
Customer submits an order with an indication to prioritize based on their fair-play score if product is limited.
Customer selects a product and initiates payment using their personal virtual wallet balance.
Customer adds funds to their virtual wallet via a supported payment method.
Customer receives a real-time alert when wallet balance is insufficient to complete a transaction.
Customer selects a pickup time and location for their ordered product.
Customer receives a notification before the scheduled pickup time to confirm or reschedule.
Customer forfeits an order if they fail to complete pickup within the allowed grace period.
Farmer submits an estimate of product availability for a given week via the system interface.
Farmer updates the availability status of a product dynamically based on stock changes.
Farmer triggers a delivery delay notification to the customer when delivery cannot be completed on time.
Farmer automatically credits the customer’s wallet with a bonus amount when delivery is not completed by deadline.
Store employee views and processes customer orders for fulfillment.
Store employee confirms payment and updates wallet status for the customer’s order.
Store employee assigns a pickup time and location for a customer’s order.
Store employee marks an order as delivered and updates customer status.
Store employee updates a customer’s fair-play score based on reliability and adherence to system rules.
Customer receives a notification when their order is modified by staff or system.
Customer receives a notification when their order is canceled due to system constraints or availability issues.
Customer receives a notification when a bonus is credited to their wallet due to delivery delays or system actions.

baselineCritiques.actors: The actors defined are appropriate for the described system, covering all key roles involved in the Ethical Purchasing Group (EPS) management process. No contradictions or omissions are observed.
baselineCritiques.highLevelGoals: The high-level goals are comprehensive and align well with the software description. They cover all key functional aspects, including product sourcing transparency, order management, payment processing, pickup scheduling, inventory tracking, delivery communication, operational efficiency for store staff, fair-play scoring, and customer feedback mechanisms. No contradictions or omissions were detected.
baselineCritiques.lowLevelGoals: The low-level goals are comprehensive and align well with the high-level goals and actors. However, there is a minor omission regarding the system's validation of minimum order quantities before confirmation, which is explicitly mentioned in the software description but not directly addressed as a functional goal for any actor.
